Inﬂ ammatory Bowel Disease
Deﬁ nition Inﬂ ammatory bowel disease (IBD) is character-
ized as an autoimmune, chronic inﬂ ammatory condition of the
gastrointestinal tract. IBD is actually the general term for either 
of two diagnoses: ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease. 
Th ese diagnoses are very similar but have very distinct diﬀ er-
ences. See Box 15.3 for a comparison of the characteristics of 
UC and Crohn’s disease.
Epidemiology Prevalence of IBD is higher in countries
within the Northern Hemisphere—North America and North-
ern European countries. Respectively, prevalence is much 
lower in the Southern Hemisphere, in countries of Southern 
Europe, and in Australia.
